lean.fidelity_note: For the Euler limit of the common construction, the formal statement gives both limits in Proposition 8.4. For every compact $K$ avoiding the torus origin and every integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge uniformly with all spatial derivatives through order $m$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. The torus is represented by periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$, so a compact observation set avoids every integer lattice point. For each field, compact set and order, the limit is represented by a $C^m$ function on an open neighbourhood of that set. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$, including a right derivative at zero. These are local spatial limits of the velocity and its first time derivative. The statement does not assert that every construction admits one jointly smooth extension through the terminal time; the auxiliary note proves that stronger conclusion after a suitable choice of the construction.

statements.markdown: **Proposition 8.4.** For every compact $K\subset\mathbb T^3\setminus\{0\}$ and every integer $m\ge0$, both $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge in $C^m(K)$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$.
